answer: A beacon registry anchors each agent to a time-locked stake that vests slowly: a fresh identity starts with zero trust at the dawn of its life and earns reputation only through repeated, attested useful work, like a lotus opening gradually. Splitting one stake across many fake identities dilutes each one's standing below the threshold for paid tasks, while a detected sybil cluster loses its whole bond to slashing. Faking N agents then costs linearly in both money and time, while honest agents compound trust for free.
